title: Antonov Airlines
summary: Antonov Airlines is a [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] cargo airline, part of the Antonov aviation company, specializing in international charter services for oversized cargo. Its primary operations were based at Hostomel Airport near [[kyiv|Kyiv]] until the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine necessitated a relocation to Leipzig/Halle Airport in Germany.

sections.heading: History
paragraphs: Antonov Airlines was founded in 1989, initially operating through a marketing agreement with Air Foyle to promote [[antonov|Antonov]] An-124 Ruslan cargo charters globally. This partnership concluded in June 2006, coinciding with the establishment of a joint venture named Rusland International with Volga-[[dnieper|Dnepr]] Airlines, where both companies held equal stakes. This collaboration allowed the sharing of a combined fleet of seventeen An-124-100 aircraft, twelve of which were owned by Antonov Airlines.
In 2017, Antonov Airlines expanded its operations by opening an office in the United Kingdom at London Stansted Airport, with its inaugural flight occurring in February of that year.

sections.heading: Impact of the 2022 Russian Invasion
paragraphs: During the onset of the [[2022-russian-invasion-of-ukraine|2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], the An-225 Mriya was at Antonov Airport in Hostomel for maintenance. The airport was captured during the Battle of Antonov Airport, resulting in the destruction of the An-225. [[ukrainian-defense-industry|UkrOboronProm]] estimated the cost of restoration to exceed 3 billion USD and projected a timeline of over five years, asserting that these costs should be borne by the Russian Federation due to the intentional damage inflicted on [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s aviation sector.

Following the invasion, remaining Antonov Airlines aircraft were redirected to Leipzig/Halle Airport after completing their commercial missions, where the airline continued operations with five An-124 aircraft.

sections.heading: Notable Operations
paragraphs: Antonov Airlines has been involved in numerous significant cargo operations, including the transport of an 88-ton water turbine for the Tashtakumska Hydroelectric Plant from [[kharkiv-oblast|Kharkiv]] to Tashkent, and civil engineering vehicles to assist with earthquake recovery efforts in Spitak, Armenia.

Other notable missions included transporting vehicles and systems for mine clearance during the Persian Gulf crisis, a 135.2-ton Siemens generator from Düsseldorf, Germany, to Delhi, India, and nuclear fuel from Habaniya, Iraq, to Yekaterinburg, Russia, under a UN disarmament program.

The airline also facilitated the delivery of a 102-ton locomotive from London, Ontario, Canada, to Dublin, Ireland, and a 70-ton generator from Doncaster Robin Hood, UK, to Lahore, Pakistan, among various other international cargo missions.

sections.heading: Fleet
paragraphs: As of August 2025, Antonov Airlines operates a fleet that includes several An-124 aircraft. However, the airline suffered significant losses during the 2022 conflict, with the destruction of three aircraft: the Antonov An-26-100 (UR-13395), Antonov An-74T-100 (UR-74010), and the Antonov An-225-100 Mriya (UR-82060).
Historically, the fleet also included various Antonov models such as the An-12, An-26, An-28, An-32, An-74, An-178, An-140, and An-148.
